whatText:
A makerspace is a shared workshop where people create, experiment, and build together—using tools that are rare, specialized, expensive, or simply too large for most individuals to own.

Most makerspaces operate in libraries, schools, or universities.

We are unique in being a membership funded non-profit organization.
offerText: Click an item to get a list of equipment in each section.
howBullets:
We are a volunteer operated **501(c)(3) non-profit**, nobody gets paid.
Everyone pitches in, whether it’s giving tours or taking out the trash
Our tool collection grows through donated and loaned gear from makers
Membership fees keep the lights on — rent, utilities, insurance, supplies, repairs, outreach
Safety first: members complete training before they’re turned loose on the machines.
reviewsText: Hear from makers who are part of our community.

reviews.name: Chris
reviews.text: Kzoo Makers is easily one of the most inspiring spaces I've encountered. The range of equipment is impressive, but what really sets it apart is the community.

reviews.name: Austin
reviews.text: As a small business owner prototyping new products, I found the makerspace invaluable. The real value comes from the people and culture of collaboration.

reviews.name: Parker
reviews.text: The biggest shift for me has been confidence in tool proficiency. At home I hesitated before every cut or print. Here, measured feedback from experienced members eliminates that uncertainty.

reviews.name: Riley
reviews.text: Before joining Kzoo Makers, most of my projects stalled out halfway. Having immediate access to people who understand fabrication workflows changed that.

reviews.name: Sam
reviews.text: I came for access to a 3D printer and ended up learning far more about electronics diagnostics than I planned. That honesty makes learning efficient instead of frustrating.

reviews.name: Lucas
reviews.text: I go to Kalamazoo Linux Users group and I use Linux, people are very friendly at The Makerspace. Thank you for listening Ryan.

reviews.name: Taylor
reviews.text: Kzoo Makers gave me my first exposure to metalworking tools that most hobbyists can't justify at home. It's one of the few places where experimentation and discipline coexist.

reviews.name: Jordan
reviews.text: I joined to prototype a product idea, and the environment forced me to confront weak points in my process. The space removes excuses and exposes gaps you didn't notice.

reviews.name: Chris
reviews.text: Experienced members are generous with their knowledge, and new makers are encouraged to dive in without intimidation. You walk in with an idea and leave with something real in your hands.

reviews.name: Avery
reviews.text: What surprised me most is the range of skills represented here. The reciprocity feels natural. It's collaborative without drifting into chaos.

reviews.name: Morgan
reviews.text: I've worked in corporate engineering labs, but accessibility was always limited. Here, the tools and space are straightforward to book. It's not just equipment—it's operational freedom.

reviews.name: Riley
reviews.text: I've gone from guesswork to deliberate iteration, especially with wood CNC and safety practices. It's the first place where my ideas stop being hypothetical.

reviews.name: Sigrid
reviews.text: I like how inclusive and creative people are here, this space is special to me because it's like my second home after the coffee shop of course!

reviews.name: James
reviews.text: I've got all this equipment at my house, but after woodworking for 33 years it's boring at home. I like how I can come in to the building and collaborate and bounce ideas off peoples heads.
